sb_prompt: DISCUSS GUN CONTROL.  WHERE DO YOU AND THE OTHER CALLER STAND ON A SCALE FROM 1 TO 10
turns: Yeah, that's what I've been thinking about. I've been electrician for years and I just think people need to be able to defend themselves, you know?

Yeah, I guess. My cousin had to go through it last year when his mom's car got into a situation, and honestly, it felt like a mess, but I don't know, he thinks having a gun is the only way to stop it.

Yeah, I get that. But honestly, I've just never seen a situation where the police couldn't get there in time or where someone didn't just shoot themselves in the foot trying to use a gun to stop a car. My gut just says it makes things worse, even if you think it's the only way.
That's a fair point, but my cousin said if you're not armed, you're already dead before the cops arrive.

I mean, that's the scary part, isn't it? You're dead before the help shows up. I work with guys who are out there every day and I just don't see that being the outcome. Most of the time I've seen, it's a bad situation all around.
Yeah, but when you're sitting right there in your own home and the cops are ten minutes out, does waiting really feel like an option?

I mean, you're sitting there thinking that, but I've seen so many situations where people just panic and do something stupid, like shoot the wrong person or get shot trying to grab a weapon they don't know how to use.
Yeah, but I get why you'd say that, I just don't think you can count on them showing up fast enough sometimes.

You know, I just never really thought about the time factor, but honestly, if you've been in my shop, you know people get into trouble all the time and they just don't want to wait for the 911 dispatcher to even hang up.

Yeah, I get that about the panic part, but if you tell me you've seen people do something stupid, does that mean you've seen them survive it in the end? Because that's the whole point for me, right? That the only way to make it to the end is to be the one holding the gun.

Yeah, but it's not about surviving the end, it's about not having to be there at all. I've seen guys who tried to grab a knife or just run and ended up dead anyway because they couldn't handle the stress, and I've seen others who put a gun away and called 911 and walked away because the perp didn't hurt anyone. It feels like a gamble to me, you know? Like you're trading one kind of danger for another, and you don't know which side of the line you're on until it's too late.

Yeah, I get that, but telling someone to just throw away the only thing that might actually stop them right now... it feels like asking them to play Russian roulette. What if the perp doesn't run? What if they come through the door and you're just sitting there waiting for a call that won't come for ten minutes? That's the part I can't wrap my head around.
Right, but you're betting your whole life on that gamble, and I just don't trust the odds when you're holding something that heavy and your hands are shaking.
That's just it, isn't it? It's not about the odds, it's about the silence. If you aren't there to stop them, who do you bet on?
Yeah, but when your hands are shaking, you don't want to be the one betting on the silence, you want to trust someone who isn't there to make a mistake.
I mean, but if you're the only one shaking and the other guy isn't, doesn't that leave you with nothing to fall back on if you decide to put the gun down?
Yeah, but if you're shaking so bad you can't aim, putting it down is the only way to not accidentally hit your own kid or your neighbor down the hall.

That's a good point about the shaking hands, but honestly, you're talking about the person who's already losing the fight because they're scared, not the person who's actually trying to stop the bad guy. And if you're the one standing there without a weapon, you aren't losing the fight, you're just the victim.

You know, that's exactly why I say it's a gamble. If you're the one shaking and you don't have a gun, you're not losing the fight yet, you're just waiting to see who else gets scared enough to hurt someone by mistake. I've seen guys get shot in their own home because they thought they had to aim, but they missed the bad guy and hit their own family. And if you're not armed, you're stuck in the middle of all that panic with nothing but a shaking hand and a phone line that takes forever to clear. It feels like asking people to trust silence when their hands are shaking so bad they can't hold anything steady.
I mean, I get the shaking hand part, but if you're already scared to aim, aren't you already in trouble just by having the weapon there in the first place?

Yeah, but you're leaving yourself open to the mistake right before the call even connects. If you're shaking so bad you can't aim, the only thing that stops you from hitting your own family is not having the gun there to start with. You can't control the silence, but you can control not holding the thing that turns the silence into a tragedy.
But honestly, if you don't have that option, who do you trust to hold it steady when the line isn't clear?

You know, I think the problem is you're looking at the guy holding the gun and thinking he's going to be steady, but I've seen too many guys who start out steady and then the moment the panic kicks in, the whole thing just goes sideways.
You're saying the panic makes them shaky, but if they don't have the gun, they don't even get that chance to stay steady—they're just sitting there waiting for someone else to fix it.
That's true, but if you're the one waiting for someone else to fix it, you're the one stuck in the middle of all the shaking while the bad guy is right there in the room.
But if the bad guy is right there in the room and you're stuck waiting for someone else to fix it, aren't you already dead before the call even connects?

I mean, that's the thing, isn't it? If you're just waiting, you're already dead, but if you're holding that thing, you're just trading one kind of dead for another, and I've seen guys do the stupid thing and end up on the wrong side of it anyway.
Yeah, but if you're stuck in the middle of all that shaking while the bad guy is right there, don't you think the smartest play is just to put the gun away before you even start?

I just mean, if you put the gun away in a panic, you're not in the middle of anything anymore, you're just standing there helpless while they walk right up to you and take everything. I've seen that happen a few times, you know?
Yeah, but if you put it down and they don't back off, you're just sitting there watching them come closer while you're too scared to move.
Yeah, but if you put it down and they don't back off, you're just sitting there watching them come closer while you're too scared to move.
Wait, so you're saying if I don't have that gun, the only thing I have is a shaking hand and a dead end?

I'm saying exactly that, but here's the kicker: I've seen guys who put the gun down and thought they were safe, and then the bad guy just walks in and takes them out because they thought they had time. And I've seen others who fired and made it out because they knew they had to make that first move before the shaking took over. It's not about being steady, it's about making sure the only thing shaking is the bad guy's nerves, not yours.

But if you're right, then it's not about being steady, it's about making sure the only thing shaking is the bad guy's nerves, not yours. That's the only way I can see it working, even if it feels like playing Russian roulette.
Yeah, that's the scary part, isn't it? You bet everything on your hands not shaking, and if they do, you don't even get the chance to make the move before the panic takes over.
Yeah, but if you're right about that, then why do so many people end up on the wrong side of the line just because they hesitated a second too long?
And that's the thing, if you hesitate just a second too long waiting for that "steady" moment, you're already in the dark before the lights even turn on.
Yeah, but if you wait for that "steady" moment to even exist, you're already lost before you can make the move.
Yeah, but if you wait for the lights to turn on, you're already in the dark, and by the time they do, it's too late.
That's the thing that makes it so hard, isn't it? You're just waiting in that dark knowing you might not have that split second before they take you out.
